title: Iron Ore Prices Recover as Seaborne Volumes Lose Momentum
section_path: Iron Ore Prices Recover as Seaborne Volumes Lose Momentum
section_path_text: Iron Ore Prices Recover as Seaborne Volumes Lose Momentum
summary:
Main
By Ulf Bergman
Iron ore prices have experienced a modest renaissance since the beginning of August. The September futures listed on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) have gained around six per cent since the beginning of last month. Still, notwithstanding the recent gains, the contracts are trading nearly ten per cent below the levels recorded in mid-May.

children.title: Iron Ore Prices Recovering from a Low Base
section_path: Iron Ore Prices Recovering from a Low Base
children.section_path_text: Iron Ore Prices Recovering from a Low Base
children.summary: After settling at 93.76 dollars per tonne, the lowest level in nearly thirteen months, at the beginning of August, the September SGX iron ore futures have been recovering some of the recent losses and are trading just below 100 dollars per tonne. The current price levels are approximately ten dollars below the high for the year, set in the middle of May.

children.title: Second-half Seaborne Iron Ore Exports off to a Soft Start
section_path: Second-half Seaborne Iron Ore Exports off to a Soft Start
children.section_path_text: Second-half Seaborne Iron Ore Exports off to a Soft Start
children.summary: Global seaborne volumes of iron ore were lower in July and August compared with the same months last year. According to data from Signal Ocean, the year-on-year decline during the former month was nearly half a per cent, while the latter saw export volumes slide by almost two per cent.

children.title: Outlook for the Remainder of the Year
section_path: Outlook for the Remainder of the Year
children.section_path_text: Outlook for the Remainder of the Year
children.summary: The slow start to the second half of the year for seaborne iron ore exports suggests that concerns over economic growth may have tempered demand. The lower volumes in recent months could also provide some limited support for prices in the short term.
